gaps.sentence: I ___ getting up early because I have done it for years.
gaps.hint: be used to means present familiarity
gaps.explanation: 'Be used to' plus -ing means familiarity with something, here in the present: am used to.

gaps.sentence: I ___ in this city since 2015, and I still love it.
gaps.hint: since 2015 plus still means it continues
gaps.explanation: 'Since 2015' with 'still' marks a situation continuing to the present, so the present perfect is used: have lived.

gaps.sentence: She ___ two majors when she was at university.
gaps.hint: a completed period in the past
gaps.explanation: A completed past period takes the past simple: did.

gaps.sentence: When you ___ John tomorrow, please give him my regards.
gaps.hint: no will after when for the future
gaps.explanation: In time clauses referring to the future, English uses the present simple, not 'will': see.

gaps.sentence: Be quiet! The baby ___ in the next room.
gaps.hint: be quiet means an action in progress
gaps.explanation: The request for quiet shows an action happening at this moment, so use the present continuous: is sleeping.

gaps.sentence: They ___ for two hours when the storm hit.
gaps.hint: two hours of walking before the storm
gaps.explanation: A duration leading up to a past moment takes the past perfect continuous: had been walking.

gaps.sentence: The conference ___ on Monday and ends on Wednesday.
gaps.explanation: Fixed schedules are stated in the present simple: starts.

gaps.sentence: When I was a boy, films ___ in black and white.
gaps.hint: a past state no longer existing
gaps.explanation: 'Used to be' describes a past state that has ended: used to be.
